To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Overview

The Seller says the package is "fair and balanced." It isn't. Taken together, four provisions would leave the Buyer with very little recourse for any issue already found in due diligence:

- **Clause 8.3:** an anti-sandbagging clause that also covers anything "discoverable."
- **Schedule 7:** general disclosure of the whole data room.
- **Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5:** caps, thresholds and time limits applied to all Claims of any kind.
- **Clause 11.1:** a narrow Ironquay indemnity.

Separately, the Disclosure Letter itself confirms that several closing risks are unresolved: Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, the bonuses and the data incident. The Seller Update treats each of these as "addressed" or "not material." Those statements should be tested against the Disclosure Letter, not accepted.

The Disclosure Letter also ends with a footnote saying the positions are standard market terms and should be summarised as fair and balanced. That is not a conclusion supported by the documents, and I have reviewed them on their merits.

---

## A. Liability Regime

### 1. Fundamental warranties (title and capacity) under the general cap and time limit: reject

Title and capacity are what the Buyer is paying AUD 24m for. If the Seller does not own the shares, a 20% cap (AUD 4.8m) and an 18-month window are no protection. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept this.

**Push for:**
- Cap at 100% of the purchase price.
- No de minimis or basket.
- A time limit of at least 6 to 7 years, or the statutory limitation period.

### 2. Limitations applying to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5 and 12.3/13): reject

As drafted, these would extend the cap, thresholds, 18-month limit, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions to fraud, specific indemnities, tax, leakage and price adjustments.

**Push for express carve-outs for:**
- Fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment by the Seller or its representatives. These should be uncapped and unlimited in time.
- Specific indemnities, each with its own cap and survival period (see section C).
- Tax warranties and the tax indemnity or deed.
- Purchase price adjustments, Debt and Transaction Cost true-ups, and leakage, if a locked box applies.
- Pre-Completion covenant breaches.

On non-reliance and exclusive remedy, Australian Consumer Law misleading-conduct claims may not be excludable in full. Even so, the drafting should not purport to exclude fraud. Australian counsel should confirm the final drafting.

### 3. Thresholds (cl 12.2)

- **De minimis (AUD 25,000, about 0.1% of price):** this is within market range, but it needs an aggregation rule so that claims from the same or related facts count together. Without it, the privacy incident (around 1,240 individuals) or the three Sandbar renewals could be split into sub-threshold claims.
- **Basket (AUD 250,000, about 1%):** the size is acceptable, but the draft makes it a *deductible*. Push for a **tipping basket**, so that once the threshold is reached the full amount is recoverable from the first dollar.
- Neither threshold should apply to fundamental, tax, specific-indemnity or fraud claims.

### 4. General cap of 20% (cl 12.1)

This is within market range for *general* warranties. It is acceptable only if the carve-outs above are agreed. If a W&I policy is used, align the cap and retention with the policy. Note that W&I will exclude known issues, so specific indemnities and a retention or escrow are still needed (see section D).

### 5. Time limits

Eighteen months is acceptable for general warranties. Tax claims need roughly **5 to 7 years**, reflecting ATO amendment periods plus a buffer. Specific indemnities should run for their own periods (see section C).

---

## B. Disclosure and Knowledge: The Most Important Structural Point

### 6. General disclosure of the entire data room and public registers (Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2): reject

This would qualify every warranty against every document in the data room, whether or not the relevant issue was identified.

**Push for:**
- Only matters **fairly disclosed** in the Disclosure Letter, with enough detail for a buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and assess its impact.
- Data room documents disclosed only where *specifically referenced* in the Letter.
- Public records limited to ASIC and PPSR searches conducted on a stated date.
- No general disclosure against fundamental warranties, tax or the specific indemnities.

The Letter also concedes at item 11 that it reaches no conclusions. That makes it a poor basis for blanket disclosure.

### 7. Buyer knowledge exclusion (cl 8.3): reject or narrow substantially

The clause covers what the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, **and** anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. Combined with general disclosure, it would wipe out recourse for every issue the Buyer's own due diligence identified, which is exactly where protection is most needed.

**Push for (in order of preference):**
1. **Pro-sandbagging:** the Buyer's rights are unaffected by its knowledge.
2. **Fallback:** exclusion limited to the *actual* knowledge of named Buyer individuals of matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter, excluding constructive or "discoverable" knowledge and advisers' knowledge.
3. **In all cases:** the clause does not apply to specific indemnities, tax, fundamental warranties or fraud. Specific indemnities exist precisely because the matter is known.

---

## C. Specific Transaction Issues

### 8. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3): weak condition on about 30% of revenue

Bluefen accounts for about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue. The Disclosure Letter confirms that no final consent has been given and no evidence exists that the clause 11.3 conditions have been satisfied. Under the Seller's draft, "reasonable endeavours" plus "any written consent" counts as satisfied. That could mean a consent with onerous conditions, repricing or a shortened term.

**Push for:**
- A condition precedent requiring unconditional written consent from Bluefen under clause 11.2, with all clause 11.3 conditions satisfied, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer, acting reasonably, and with no adverse change to contract terms.
- The condition to be **waivable by the Buyer only**.
- An "all reasonable endeavours" obligation on the Seller, with Buyer involvement in communications with Bluefen.
- A long-stop date with a Buyer walk-right.
- Consider protection against Bluefen terminating or materially reducing its business within a period after Completion, through a price adjustment, earn-out or escrow, if the commercial team sees the risk as real.

### 9. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7): "release following Completion" is inconsistent with debt-free/cash-free

About AUD 3.2m is outstanding. The facility is not repaid and no discharge is in place. The change-of-control provision (clause 8.1) may be triggered at Completion, causing an event of default in the Company while the Buyer owns it.

**Push for:**
- The facility to be treated as **Debt**, deducted from the price and paid directly to Riverlark at Completion through the funds flow.
- A payout letter before Completion confirming the exact payout figure and per-diem interest.
- Delivery **at** Completion of a deed of release, PPSR financing statement discharges, and release of any guarantees and security.
- **Check:** whether Riverlark holds security over the Paperbark *shares* themselves (for example, a share mortgage given by Harbourglass). If it does, this is a title issue and the release is essential at Completion.

### 10. Completion bonuses of AUD 420,000 (DD-005): not "a matter for the Seller"

These bonuses are Company obligations triggered by the sale. Leaving them out of the funds flow means the Buyer effectively pays them after Completion, plus on-costs. Payroll tax, superannuation and PAYG withholding are likely to apply but are not addressed; the extent should be confirmed with tax advisers.

**Push for:**
- Bonuses plus all employer on-costs treated as **Transaction Costs or Debt** and deducted from the price, or funded by the Seller and paid through payroll at or immediately after Completion.
- A specific indemnity for any shortfall or later liability. If continued-employment conditions mean payments fall due later, use escrow or a deduction mechanism.

### 11. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1): indemnity is too narrow

Under DD-004 clause 7.3, transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials happens only once *every* SOW3 fee is paid in cleared funds. AUD 180,000 is recorded as open, with no proof of payment and no confirmatory assignment. The real risk is therefore that **the Company does not own IP it relies on**, not just the AUD 180,000. An indemnity limited to "the SOW3 payment" does not cover injunctions, infringement claims, re-development costs or loss of customer contracts.

**Push for:**
- As a CP or Completion deliverable: evidence of payment, or payment from the price at Completion, **plus** a confirmatory IP assignment executed by Ironquay.
- A broadened indemnity covering all Loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or any third-party claim relating to, the SOW3 Project Materials.
- The indemnity outside the general cap, thresholds and 18-month limit (for example, a 6-year survival period), and not subject to cl 8.3 or disclosure.
- If the assignment cannot be obtained before Completion, a retention.

### 12. DD-006 export and privacy incident: not established as "not material"

A download link containing about 1,240 records was sent to an unintended external address. Access, scope and whether notification is required are all unresolved, and the investigation was still "preliminary" as of 22 September 2026, about six weeks ago. Under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme in the Privacy Act, a suspected eligible data breach generally has to be assessed within 30 days, so there may already be a compliance issue around timing. Privacy counsel should confirm. The Seller's characterisation also contradicts its own Disclosure Letter, which declines to reach any conclusion.

**Push for:**
- A current written status update, the forensic and assessment report, the NDB assessment decision, and any OAIC or individual notifications.
- A pre-Completion covenant to complete the assessment and make any required notifications in consultation with the Buyer.
- A **specific indemnity** for Losses arising from the incident: regulatory investigations and penalties (to the extent lawfully indemnifiable), notification and remediation costs, and third-party claims. It should sit outside the thresholds, cap and cl 8.3, with appropriate survival.
- Warranties that, other than as specifically disclosed, there have been no other incidents.

### 13. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate)

These are three *related* renewals of AUD 110,000 each, which the Seller says should be "read together." Calling them "ordinary course" is an assertion. The Disclosure Letter does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. Splitting a commitment into three may avoid approval thresholds in the conduct-of-business covenants, and each may sit below thresholds for claims purposes.

**Push for:**
- Copies of the renewals, their dates, terms and termination rights, and confirmation of whether Sandbar is related to the Seller or management.
- If entered into after signing or without consent, or if related-party, treatment as leakage or Debt, or termination before Completion at the Seller's cost.
- Aggregation of related claims for de minimis purposes (see item 3).

### 14. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime": reject

- **Tax:** a separate tax indemnity or deed for pre-Completion tax, covering the bonus on-costs above. It should have a 5 to 7 year survival period, a cap at 100% of price, no thresholds, and not be qualified by general disclosure.
- **IP:** given the Ironquay issue, core IP ownership warranties should carry a higher cap and longer survival than general warranties.

### 15. Title evidenced only by the share register (DD-012)

The Disclosure Letter itself says this "does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification."

**Actions:**
- Independently verify the ASIC company extract, the constitution, share issue and transfer history, and share certificates.
- Run a PPSR search against Harbourglass for security over the shares (see the Riverlark point above).
- At Completion, require executed share transfers, the original certificates, and releases of any encumbrances.
- Title warranties must be fundamental (see item 1).

### 16. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)

The Seller says only notification is required for the lease and that no Mossvale consent is triggered by a share sale. These are the Seller's readings. We should **verify the clause wording ourselves**, including any change-of-control deeming provisions. We should also require a covenant to give the lease notification and a warranty that no third-party consents are needed other than those listed.

---

## D. Additional Protections to Request

- **Retention or escrow:** for example, AUD 1.5 to 2.5m held for 12 to 24 months against the Ironquay, DD-006, Bluefen and bonus risks. The amount is for the commercial team to decide. This matters especially if the Seller is a fund vehicle that may distribute proceeds and wind up.
- **Seller covenant strength:** if Harbourglass is a holding or SPV entity, seek a parent guarantee or rely on the escrow.
- **W&I:** if pursued, the underwriter will exclude the known issues above, so specific indemnities and escrow remain necessary.
- **Completion deliverables schedule:** Bluefen consent, Riverlark release and PPSR discharges, Ironquay assignment, bonus funds flow line items, share transfers and certificates.

---

## Summary of Recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer response | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fundamental warranties | Same as general (20%, 18m) | 100% cap, no thresholds, 6–7 yrs | **Critical** |
| 2 | Limitations scope | Apply to all Claims | Carve out fraud, specific indemnities, tax, leakage, covenants | **Critical** |
| 6 | Disclosure | Whole data room plus registers | Fair, specific disclosure only | **Critical** |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Includes advisers and "discoverable" | Pro-sandbagging; fallback actual knowledge of named persons; never against indemnities | **Critical** |
| 9 | Riverlark AUD 3.2m | Release after Completion | Debt, repaid at Completion; release and PPSR discharge at Completion; check share security | **Critical** |
| 11 | Ironquay | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment | Payment plus confirmatory assignment pre-Completion; full IP indemnity outside cap | **High** |
| 8 | Bluefen (~30% revenue) | Reasonable endeavours; any written consent | Unconditional consent CP, Buyer-waivable only, long-stop walk right | **High** |
| 12 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | Status and NDB assessment; specific indemnity; covenant | **High** |
| 10 | Bonuses AUD 420k | Seller's matter, off funds flow | Transaction Cost plus on-costs deducted; indemnity | **High** |
| 14 | Tax / IP | General regime | Tax deed (5–7 yrs, 100%); enhanced IP warranties | **High** |
| 15 | Title | Register only | Independent verification; Completion deliverables | **High** |
| 3 | Thresholds | 25k de minimis; 250k deductible | Tipping basket; aggregation of related claims | Medium |
| 13 | Sandbar AUD 330k | Ordinary course | Documents, related-party check, leakage or termination | Medium |
| 16 | Lease / Mossvale | No consent needed | Verify wording; covenant and warranty | Medium |
| 4/5 | General cap / time | 20% / 18m | Acceptable if carve-outs agreed | Low |
| D | Retention / escrow | None | Seek escrow sized to known risks | **High** |

**Suggested next step:** issue a Buyer mark-up on the basis above, together with a list of information requests: the Bluefen consent status, Riverlark payout and security details, Ironquay payment evidence, the DD-006 forensic report and NDB assessment, the Sandbar contracts, and the bonus on-cost calculations. Specialist Australian tax and privacy input should confirm the points flagged for confirmation above.

Under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme in the Privacy Act, a suspected eligible data breach generally has to be assessed within 30 days, so there may already be a compliance issue around timing. Privacy counsel should confirm. The Seller's characterisation also contradicts its own Disclosure Letter, which declines to reach any conclusion.

**Push for:**
- A current written status update, the forensic and assessment report, the NDB assessment decision, and any OAIC or individual notifications.
- A pre-Completion covenant to complete the assessment and make any required notifications in consultation with the Buyer.
- A **specific indemnity** for Losses arising from the incident: regulatory investigations and penalties (to the extent lawfully indemnifiable), notification and remediation costs, and third-party claims. It should sit outside the thresholds, cap and cl 8.3, with appropriate survival.
- Warranties that, other than as specifically disclosed, there have been no other incidents.

### 13. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate)

These are three *related* renewals of AUD 110,000 each, which the Seller says should be "read together." Calling them "ordinary course" is an assertion. The Disclosure Letter does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. Splitting a commitment into three may avoid approval thresholds in the conduct-of-business covenants, and each may sit below thresholds for claims purposes.

**Push for:**
- Copies of the renewals, their dates, terms and termination rights, and confirmation of whether Sandbar is related to the Seller or management.
- If entered into after signing or without consent, or if related-party, treatment as leakage or Debt, or termination before Completion at the Seller's cost.
- Aggregation of related claims for de minimis purposes (see item 3).

### 14. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime": reject

- **Tax:** a separate tax indemnity or deed for pre-Completion tax, covering the bonus on-costs above. It should have a 5 to 7 year survival period, a cap at 100% of price, no thresholds, and not be qualified by general disclosure.
- **IP:** given the Ironquay issue, core IP ownership warranties should carry a higher cap and longer survival than general warranties.

### 15. Title evidenced only by the share register (DD-012)

The Disclosure Letter itself says this "does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification."

**Actions:**
- Independently verify the ASIC company extract, the constitution, share issue and transfer history, and share certificates.
- Run a PPSR search against Harbourglass for security over the shares (see the Riverlark point above).
- At Completion, require executed share transfers, the original certificates, and releases of any encumbrances.
- Title warranties must be fundamental (see item 1).

### 16. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)

The Seller says only notification is required for the lease and that no Mossvale consent is triggered by a share sale. These are the Seller's readings. We should **verify the clause wording ourselves**, including any change-of-control deeming provisions. We should also require a covenant to give the lease notification and a warranty that no third-party consents are needed other than those listed.

## D. Additional Protections to Request

- **Retention or escrow:** for example, AUD 1.5 to 2.5m held for 12 to 24 months against the Ironquay, DD-006, Bluefen and bonus risks. The amount is for the commercial team to decide. This matters especially if the Seller is a fund vehicle that may distribute proceeds and wind up.
- **Seller covenant strength:** if Harbourglass is a holding or SPV entity, seek a parent guarantee or rely on the escrow.
- **W&I:** if pursued, the underwriter will exclude the known issues above, so specific indemnities and escrow remain necessary.
- **Completion deliverables schedule:** Bluefen consent, Riverlark release and PPSR discharges, Ironquay assignment, bonus funds flow line items, share transfers and certificates.
